blockers: codex has required edits: Bring `pylae-verify-bootstrap` inside the PD-001 no-listener enforcement boundary. Make the supported entrypoint a static, hermetic, loader-independent artifact with an audited custom entrypoint that installs the inherited arch-gated seccomp filter before any potentially listener-capable code or descendant executes, then performs launcher verification and sealed-memfd `fexecve`; an equivalent kernel-enforced design is acceptable.; Extend the complete executable-closure definition, native capability review, packaged-artifact inspection, boot-order claims, and adversarial regressions to cover `pylae-verify-bootstrap` itself. Reconcile the current claim that only the static sandbox-builder executes before the authenticated root with the bootstrap’s earlier execution, and prove preload/loader substitution plus direct and indirect listener attempts from the bootstrap are denied.

codex has hard stops: The supported user-facing `pylae` process begins in `pylae-verify-bootstrap` before the native launcher installs seccomp, yet the bootstrap is only independently pinned/operator-trusted and is not specified as static, hermetic, filter-first, or included in the listener-capability closure. A digest proves identity, not absence of listener capability—the exact principle the plan applies to the launcher and sandbox-builder. Consequently, authentic-but-defective bootstrap code, or its pre-entry dynamic loader/library closure, can open a listener before enforcement while still executing inside the supported pylae process tree, contradicting PD-001’s stated process-tree boundary and the boot-order claim.
